Subject: Private VPC connection options — clarifying PrivateLink vs Peering and allowlist

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track items before the NetOps handoff: 

Summary from call
- CloudLedger preference: keep data in a customer-managed VPC and restrict egress.
- Initial target workload: model inference for document ingestion + interactive chat (approx. 200 qps peak, ~40 concurrent streams).
- Primary concerns: egress IPs, private connectivity pattern (PrivateLink vs VPC peering), and CA/TLS requirements for mutual auth.

Redwood recommended path (based on what we discussed)
1) Private VPC deployment (Redwood Private) — best for strict isolation and auditability.
2) PrivateLink for public endpoint ingestion if CloudLedger wants minimal route changes on their side; VPC peering can be used for tight intra-VPC traffic with lower per-request overhead.
3) We can provision static egress IPs (or small CIDR blocks) for allowlisting; alternatively use a NAT egress through your own transit if you prefer (we can document both).

Action items I need from your side to advance qualification
- Confirm network contact for the handoff (name + email).
- Confirm which connectivity you prefer (PrivateLink, VPC peering, or hybrid).
- Provide a short list of firewall rules/ports you need from us (if you have a template, great — we attached ours).
- Estimated QPS/concurrency and any SLA concerns (timeouts, burst expectations).

Attachments included: Redwood_Private_VPC_Checklist.pdf (checklist), networking_template.xlsx (example allowlist/template).

Proposed next steps
- If ok, we schedule a NetOps-to-NetOps call next week — suggest Tue/Wed (US mornings).
- Once network contact is assigned, Ben (cc'd) will respond with the egress CIDRs we propose and TLS/mTLS options.

Thanks — I’ll stand up the preliminary security questionnaire answers while we sort network details.

Sergio Alvarez

Anna — thanks for the rapid answers and for the diagram. A few technical clarifications and options from our infra side: 

Short answers
- Yes — we can publish small egress CIDR blocks for allowlisting. We typically reserve /28 blocks for customers doing strict allowlists.
- Default connectivity options supported: PrivateLink, VPC peering, or a hybrid where control plane traffic uses PrivateLink and heavy data egress uses peering.
- Ports: we only require outbound 443 for TLS traffic; health checks use TCP 10256 internally if you deploy peering + host-level checks (we can avoid host-level checks if necessary).
- TLS/mTLS: we support standard TLS with a Redwood-provided certificate chain, and can support mutual TLS (client certs) for the control plane if you require it.

Proposed egress CIDRs (provisional; final set will be assigned to your deployment region and included in the NetOps handoff)
- 34.82.160.0/28
- 35.203.120.0/28

Notes on connectivity choices
- PrivateLink pros: minimal route changes on CloudLedger side, good isolation, faster to enable across multiple accounts.
- Peering pros: slightly lower latency and fewer intermediaries for heavy throughput; requires route table updates and potential cross-account peering approvals.
- Hybrid: useful when you want to keep control-plane (billing, logs) on PrivateLink but route model-serving traffic through peering for performance.

If PrivateLink is your preference, we’ll need the following from your NetOps before the call:
- VPC name and AWS account ID(s) for each environment you want to connect.
- Security group rules where PrivateLink interface endpoints will be placed (we can provide a recommendation).
- Window for a short connectivity test once we provision the service (15–30 minute window).

I’ll draft these as checklist items and share in the NetOps handoff doc. Happy to do a quick NetOps-to-NetOps session — propose Wed 6/18 09:00 PT or Thu 6/19 10:00 PT.

-ben
